messages:
Sam Chen: FYI customer Clara Ruiz reporting 502/504s hitting Hosted API for tenant t-ACME during a bulk upload. Happening ~10:23 UTC, recurring for ~15m. They've attached curl repro and trace-id header.

Clara Ruiz: Repro steps I ran: 1) POST /v1/generate with 10 parallel connections of 2MB payloads (multipart-ish). 2) Get intermittent 502s and some 504 timeouts. Sample curl below.

Clara Ruiz: ```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Tenant-ID: t-ACME' --data-binary @chunk.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# response: HTTP/2 502
# x-trace-id: 01H7ZKQ2-abc123
```

Sam Chen: Logs from our side show edge returning 502 before request reaches model pool for those traces. Example from frontdoor logs: 

Lina Zhao: can you paste the edge log lines? Even one line with upstream status helps.

Sam Chen: snippet: 

```
[1822223333] INFO edge proxy: incoming conn from 10.4.5.6 tenant=t-ACME method=POST path=/v1/generate content-length=2048000
[1822223334] WARN env: upstream request failed status=502 upstream_host=ingress-mid-12 reason="connection reset by peer" trace=01H7ZKQ2-abc123
[1822223335] WARN env: stream closed before response produced
```

Morgan Lee: Oncall looking. Initial hypothesis: h2 connection pool to midproxy is saturated during bursts from the tenant. Any recent config changes to keepalive or connpool?

Alex Gomez: No config changes in last 48h. We did enable a limited batching rollout for embeddings yesterday but that shouldn't touch frontdoor. Also checking LB metrics now.

Priya Patel: Customer reports payloads are chunked JSON arrays ~2MB each, 10 parallel. That can push a lot of concurrent streams. Could be h2 stream window exhaustion or upstream idle timeout.

Lina Zhao: Quick check: are those 502s correlated with auth service latency? If auth/token check stalls, frontdoor can hit proxy timeouts. Sam, can you grep auth latencies for the same traces?

Sam Chen: Auth latencies for trace 01H7ZKQ2-abc123: 120ms (ok). But I see repeated `upstream reset` patterns for many traces within 10:23-10:38. Correlating with p95 connections on ingress-mid-12 spiked from 200->900.

Alex Gomez: I'm seeing upstream pool exhaustion alerts firing at 10:24 (ingress-mid-12). There are also many RST_STREAM from upstream host. Likely connection window/queue saturation.

Priya Patel: Actionable next steps: 1) ask customer to drop parallelism to 2-3 and retry to confirm. 2) We should temporarily increase h2 pool size on ingress-mid-12 and add a short conn retry policy. 3) Add temporary route fallback to lower-cost model to reduce load if pool saturated.

Sam Chen: I told Clara to reduce parallelism and send back results. She replied: "dropping to 3 parallel eliminated 502s in my test" :thumbsup:.

Morgan Lee: Good repro. I'll open an infra ticket to scale h2 pool and adjust timeouts. Alex/Lina can you create the midproxy scaling runbook and schedule a short autoscale bump. Also add a synthetic burst test on staging to repro safely.

Lina Zhao: On it. I'll also instrument prefix/KV cache hitrate to see if cache miss storm contributed.

Alex Gomez: Creating runbook now, linking to this thread. deploy-bot: started incident-ops runbook creation.

deploy-bot: Incident runbook created: IR-2026-473, linked -> https://internal.runbooks/incidents/IR-2026-473

Sam Chen: Summary for ticket: Tenant t-ACME caused h2 upstream pool saturation with large parallel chunked uploads, resulting in upstream RSTs and edge 502/504s. Mitigation: customer reduced parallelism (confirmed), infra to scale midproxy pools and add short-term retry/fallback.

Priya Patel: We'll follow up with Clara on recommended client-side concurrency limits and add guidance to docs for large batch uploads.

Clara Ruiz: Thanks team — happy to test any changes on our end and confirm once infra bump is in place."
